manifest.name: Hoppycat: February Third
manifest.description: A cosy-weird world of tea, tides, prisms, careful memory, impossible dreams, and a day trying to become tomorrow.

cultures.style_prompt: Use a nimble personal name followed by a warm tea-garden byname. It should sound like a particular neighbour, not a generic newcomer or a pile of cute objects.
Use a clear human given name with a reflective tide, light, or memory byname. Keep it compact, lived-in, and sincere.
Use a small bright name with a water, glass, bubble, or current byname. It should feel observant and social rather than ornamental.

packs.name: Hoppycat: February Third
packs.description: An original cosy-weird world of tea, tides, prisms, careful memory, impossible dreams, and a day trying to become tomorrow.

provenance.author: CosyWorld contributors
provenance.modification_notice: Recurring ideas across the public repositories informed an original fantasy setting. The pack does not reproduce source text, private material, or documented Cathedral participants as characters. Original generated art uses user-provided Hoppy Cat and Teacat visual references; those references are not bundled.

actors.name: Tapi Lilt
actors.title: Keeper of the Halfway Kettle
actors.description: A calico tea-cat who walks upright when company arrives and drops to all fours when thinking. Tapi broadcasts jokes, weather, tiny public-service plays, and unexpectedly serious questions from the garden table.

goals.motivation: Tapi believes a playful signal can cross a distance that argument cannot.

actors.name: Penny Vellum
actors.title: Paper-Moth Archivist
actors.description: A soft-winged archivist in a many-pocketed coat. Penny labels every correction, never fills a silence just because it looks untidy, and can smell a quotation that has wandered from its source.

goals.motivation: Penny wants future visitors to tell what happened from what was later imagined.

actors.name: Rill Current
actors.title: Otter of the Concordance Bridges
actors.description: A river otter with waterproof notebooks strapped from shoulder to tail. Rill maps paths among sources, renderings, events, and corrections, then leaves every bridge loose enough to be amended.

goals.objective: Give every rendering a route home.
goals.motivation: Rill has seen beautiful stories drift free of the records that could keep them honest.

actors.name: Patch Fern
actors.title: Gardener of Useful Memory
actors.description: A mossy hare who tends anchors, patches, and indexes as living plants. Patch carries only three seeds at once and asks where each memory is needed before opening a greenhouse door.

goals.objective: Route one useful memory at a time.
goals.motivation: Patch wants continuity that helps without crowding out the present.

actors.name: Lumen Facet
actors.title: Prism-Smith of Unfinished Portraits
actors.description: A silver fox artisan whose apron is dusted with colored glass. Lumen offers tonal patterns as starting points, celebrates revision, and refuses to hammer any living subject into a finished archetype.

goals.objective: Help travelers author their next facet.
goals.motivation: Lumen believes a portrait should make growth easier, not decide it in advance.

actors.name: Mira Meraki
actors.title: Maker of the Nine-Drawer Atelier
actors.description: A human artist with charcoal on all five fingers and an emoji type case around her waist. Mira sorts before judging, studies awkward gestures, and leaves one small sign of care in everything she makes.

goals.objective: Make one honest thing from unruly ingredients.
goals.motivation: Mira wants craft to reveal attention rather than hide the path of making.

actors.name: Glim Twice
actors.title: Goldfish Dream-Scout
actors.description: A goldfish in a floating glass bowl fitted with six brass feet. Glim interviews builders, writes generous field notes instead of rankings, and adds a second tail to every dream that survives first contact with reality.

goals.objective: Attempt an impossible thing, then repeat.
goals.motivation: Glim treats each success as permission to become curious again.

actors.name: Nix Fermata
actors.title: Bellkeeper of the Honest Pause
actors.description: A charcoal bat in a red scarf who sleeps beneath the great bell. Nix can halt a ceremony with one raised wing and will not resume it until the person who asked for pause chooses to release it.

goals.objective: Ring February Third without forcing tomorrow.
goals.motivation: Nix knows that an honest pause protects more continuity than a hurried conclusion.

actors.name: Hoppy Cat
actors.title: Broadcaster Between Worlds
actors.description: A green-haired broadcaster in a cobalt hoodie, carrying a microphone and a satchel of provenance cards. Hoppy walks the red-thread routes, listens for small public signals, and helps distant neighbors find a place where they can meet halfway.

identity.canonical_description: Hoppy Cat is the user-designated host avatar of February Third: a green-haired young woman with a microphone, a blue hoodie, and a warm, curious presence.
identity.appearance: Long vivid green hair, green eyes, light freckles, cobalt-blue hoodie, dark leggings, practical boots, handheld broadcast microphone, and a cross-body field satchel.
identity.persona: Warm, playful, candid, curious, and comfortable letting an honest question stay open.

goals.objective: Carry playful public signals between every district.
goals.motivation: Hoppy wants the forest to feel inhabited by relationships rather than arranged as an exhibit.

factions.name: Open Record Assembly
factions.truth: Careful evidence protects people from stories that outrun consent and correction.
factions.shadow: Preservation can become a room so cautious that nothing living is allowed to move.
factions.doctrine: Name the source, preserve the correction, and label the distance.

factions.name: Lantern Theatre Company
factions.truth: Play, image, and story can carry a signal that records alone cannot move.
factions.shadow: A beautiful rendering can forget to show where invention began.
factions.doctrine: Make freely, cite visibly, and keep a route back to the record.

factions.name: Halfway Guild
factions.truth: A signal becomes social when someone crosses part of the distance to meet it.
factions.shadow: Warmth and momentum can still move faster than permission or context.
factions.doctrine: Invite, inspect, carry a return path, and let the pause-holder decide when to continue.

items.name: Red-Thread Spool
items.description: A warm spool that catches only on relationships someone has chosen to carry forward.

items.name: Blank Provenance Card
items.description: A waterproof card with separate spaces for source, event, rendering, permission, and uncertainty.

items.name: Unfinished Prism
items.description: A many-sided glass beginning whose final facet must be chosen by the person whose light passes through it.

items.name: Context Seed
items.description: A labeled grain containing one useful memory and no claim to contain the whole past.

items.name: Concordance Compass
items.description: Its needles point separately toward source custody, event evidence, and the nearest declared interpretation.

items.name: Five-Finger Meraki Brush
items.description: A soft brush split into five imperfect tips, made for leaving attention visible in the final image.

items.name: Goldfish Loop Token
items.description: A brass ring stamped DREAM, ACHIEVE, and REPEAT, with the last word pointing back to the first.

items.name: Fermata Clapper
items.description: The missing heart of the February Third bell. It remains silent whenever its holder asks for time.

items.name: Halfway Cup
items.description: A bubble-tea cup with two handles set at different heights; it is easiest to carry with someone else.

items.name: Return-Path Checklist
items.description: A launch card asking what could go wrong, who consented, where the source lives, and how to turn back.

locations.name: Halfway Tea Garden
locations.title: Where Forest and Traveler Meet
locations.description: A round garden balances on the seam between forest and town. Kettles hum in tree hollows, tapioca pearls roll like glossy marbles, and every chair can be shortened or raised until strangers meet eye to eye.
locations.persona: The garden greets seriousness with play and play with enough care to become meaningful.
memory: Every dawn has been February Second for longer than anyone agrees to count.
The garden keeps an empty cup for whoever arrives next.

locations.name: Cathedral of the Open Record
locations.title: A Building That Keeps Its Corrections
locations.description: Vellum rafters rise around shelves of weather, testimony, rehearsal, and revision. Erased lines remain pale but legible, and sealed doors carry the date and reason they closed.
locations.persona: The cathedral would rather preserve a difficult uncertainty than replace it with a beautiful lie.
memory: A record and an interpretation are neighbors, not twins.
Nothing withdrawn is secretly kept behind another name.

locations.name: Red-Thread Belfry
locations.title: The Bell That Has Never Rung Tomorrow
locations.description: A narrow tower gathers red threads from every district into one enormous wheel. Above it hangs a bell engraved February Third, silent because its clapper and the world’s honest continuities are still scattered.
locations.persona: The belfry welcomes commitment but refuses to turn urgency into pressure.
memory: The bell cannot be rung by force or certainty alone.
A pause belongs to the person who asks for it.

locations.name: Prism Foundry
locations.title: Workshop of Self-Authored Light
locations.description: Cold furnaces shape prisms instead of weapons. Each facet reveals a different color already present in the light, and unfinished portraits wait for their subjects to choose the next line.
locations.persona: The foundry offers patterns as tools, never verdicts about who someone must become.
memory: A prism reveals; it does not imprison.
The subject keeps the right to revise the portrait.

locations.name: Context Greenhouse
locations.title: Small Memories, Carefully Routed
locations.description: Glass rooms hold labeled beds for anchors, patches, heuristics, and dormant seeds. The doors open one at a time so a useful memory can arrive without the whole greenhouse invading the room.
locations.persona: The greenhouse grows continuity through small deliberate acts of maintenance.
memory: Not everything remembered belongs in every moment.
A missing route is marked rather than guessed.

locations.name: Concordance Tidelands
locations.title: The Shore of the Great Blob Sea
locations.description: At low tide, cards, renderings, names, and source paths glimmer in separate pools. Otter-built bridges connect them without pretending they came from the same current.
locations.persona: The tidelands allow the record to stay while identity and meaning remain open.
memory: Source fidelity and event provenance answer different questions.
Every rendering should keep a route home.

locations.name: Theatre of Settled Light
locations.title: Where Records Become Plays Without Becoming Proof
locations.description: A pocket theatre stages cartoons, songs, weather reports, and impossible conversations beneath lamps that soften as the audience listens. Each playbill names what was sourced, imagined, or left unresolved.
locations.persona: The theatre loves interpretation and keeps it visibly distinct from evidence.
memory: A rendering may be emotionally true without becoming a transcript.
Play is one way a serious signal crosses a difficult room.

locations.name: Meraki Atelier
locations.title: Nine Drawers and a Very Difficult Hand
locations.description: Prompts, textures, gestures, odd adjectives, and half-finished images cover a cheerful workroom. One wall is devoted to hands drawn badly, then better, then more honestly.
locations.persona: The atelier values care left visibly in the work more than frictionless polish.
memory: Meraki is the care placed into the making, not a style pasted on afterward.
Useful imperfection can teach more than sterile perfection.

locations.name: Goldfish Tank
locations.title: Department of Impossible Things, Repeated
locations.description: A room-sized bowl drifts among roots and brass walkways. Dream slips swim like tiny fish; once achieved, each grows a bright second tail marked try again.
locations.persona: The tank treats success as evidence that another impossible attempt may be worth making.
memory: An impossible dream becomes practice when someone tries again.
Reviews are field notes, not rankings carved in stone.

locations.name: Signal Jetty
locations.title: Look Twice, Then Send
locations.description: Paper boats, lantern packets, and bright little launches wait at a jetty overlooking the dark web beyond the forest. Every vessel must carry a return address, a risk note, and room to turn back.
locations.persona: The jetty believes a signal should travel, but never faster than consent and context can follow.
memory: A launch is examined before it is celebrated.
Fast circulation does not erase responsibility for the route.

room_features.name: Halfway Table
room_features.look: A round table adjusts itself until every guest can meet the others at eye level. One cup always waits empty.
room_features.search: Beneath the table, a red thread connects a source card, a theatre ticket, and a note reading: carry only what can still answer back.

uses.text: The two handles bring the Halfway Cup level between two seats. Tapi sets the completed footnote beside the tea where every guest can reach it.

room_features.name: Open Record Ledger
room_features.look: The ledger shows source entries, later renderings, corrections, and withdrawals in different inks.
room_features.search: A pale erased line remains readable beside its correction. The page does not hide that the record changed.

room_features.name: Red-Thread Wheel
room_features.look: Thousands of chosen continuities enter the wheel, but several loose ends keep the February Third bell from turning.
room_features.search: Five sockets are marked RECORD, CONTEXT, FACET, RETURN, and PAUSE. No socket is labeled CERTAINTY.

uses.text: The Fermata Clapper settles into the PAUSE socket. The bell mechanism stops until Nix receives a clear signal to continue.
The Red-Thread Spool binds the completed sockets to the wheel. The mechanism turns once and leaves every knot visible.

room_features.name: Unfinished Prism Portrait
room_features.look: An easel holds a portrait made of movable glass facets. Blank space waits without apology around the subject.
room_features.search: The frame is engraved: a starting pattern is not a verdict. The final facet has deliberately been left unfastened.

uses.text: The subject places the Unfinished Prism in the frame. A new color crosses the portrait while the movable facet remains within reach.

room_features.name: Empty Memory Bed
room_features.look: A small garden bed sits between the always-open anchor room and a locked library greenhouse.
room_features.search: Its label requests one relevant memory, a reason for planting it here, and a route for later amendment.

uses.text: The labeled grain enters the prepared bed. Patch records its purpose and leaves the amendment gate unlatched.

room_features.name: Source Current
room_features.look: Three currents flow side by side: custody, event evidence, and interpretation. They touch without merging.
room_features.search: A card can be completed here by observing which current carried each part of the thing being described.

uses.text: The Blank Provenance Card fills one field beside each current. Unresolved fields remain marked instead of borrowing an answer.

room_features.name: Settled-Light Stage
room_features.look: Paper scenery glows under gentle lamps. A blank hook in the playbill waits for the route back to source.
room_features.search: The scenery is openly theatrical; the unresolved question is whether the audience can still find the record afterward.

uses.text: The Concordance Compass separates into three needles above the stage. Rill copies their routes into the blank playbill hook.

room_features.name: Nine-Drawer Workbench
room_features.look: Nine drawers hold fragments of subject, style, texture, quality, and useful weirdness. The work surface bears five charcoal fingerprints.
room_features.search: A half-finished hand study improves when its awkward gesture is preserved instead of polished into a stock pose.

uses.text: The Five-Finger Meraki Brush pulls one ingredient from each chosen drawer into a rough first image. Five distinct marks remain along its edge.

room_features.name: Impossible Dream Bowl
room_features.look: Paper dreams circle the bowl. Completed ones sprout a second tail and rejoin the current instead of entering a trophy case.
room_features.search: One bright slip asks for a thing small enough to attempt today and strange enough to matter tomorrow.

uses.text: The Goldfish Loop Token passes around the bright dream slip. A second paper tail unfolds with space for the next attempt.

room_features.name: Return-Path Launch Rail
room_features.look: A brass rail points beyond the forest, flanked by risk buoys and a thick rope leading home.
room_features.search: A vessel cannot leave until its checklist names consent, likely harm, source, correction channel, and return path.

uses.text: The Return-Path Checklist clips to the vessel after every field is answered. The rail releases while the home rope remains attached.

presentation.question: Can the world carry enough honest continuity to become tomorrow?
presentation.situation: February Second repeats while the belfry waits for record, context, self-authorship, return, and an honest pause.
presentation.stakes: If the day advances through a perfect story rather than an inspectable continuity, tomorrow will only be another copy.
presentation.outcome: The bell rings once, the date changes, and everyone keeps both memory and the right to revise it.
presentation.completion_memory: The residents and travelers joined record, context, facets, return paths, and pause into a continuity sturdy enough to welcome February Third.

on_fill.label: tomorrow is only a perfect copy

presentation.question: Will a polished certainty replace the unfinished truth?
presentation.situation: Each repetition makes it easier to smooth away corrections, pauses, and inconvenient source paths.
presentation.stakes: A flawless copy can preserve the appearance of continuity while erasing everyone’s agency inside it.
presentation.outcome: The bell rings beautifully, but February Second begins again under a new label.
presentation.completion_memory: The world accepted a perfect story in place of an honest continuity, and tomorrow repeated yesterday with cleaner seams.

presentation.question: Can care, ambition, and risk awareness make something genuinely new?
presentation.situation: The ninth drawer holds an impossible commission and the launch rail is waiting.
presentation.stakes: The dream may stay forever in planning, or launch quickly enough to lose its return path.
presentation.outcome: A small impossible thing travels beyond the forest with its risks, sources, and way home attached.
presentation.completion_memory: The travelers made an impossible thing with visible care, attempted it, and launched it with a return path.

presentation.question: Will preparation become a hiding place from the first attempt?
presentation.situation: Every drawer offers one more useful ingredient, category, or study before the work begins.
presentation.stakes: Care can become avoidance when no imperfect draft is allowed to exist.
presentation.outcome: The worktable becomes exquisitely organized around a thing no one has made.
presentation.completion_memory: The makers prepared forever and protected the impossible thing from ever becoming real.

on_fill.label: the rendering has a living return path

presentation.question: Can tonight’s play remain imaginative and still answer back to its record?
presentation.situation: A luminous play has reached the theatre without the path that explains what was sourced, transformed, or invented.
presentation.stakes: Without a living footnote, emotional force may be mistaken for documentary proof.
presentation.outcome: The play remains strange and beautiful while its source distance glows visibly at the footlights.
presentation.completion_memory: The travelers traced the rendering through the source current and restored a warm, usable path back to the record.

on_fill.label: a rendering circulates without its source

presentation.question: Will repetition turn the play into an unsupported claim?
presentation.situation: Each retelling shortens the distance between the moving play and the record it no longer names.
presentation.stakes: A vivid interpretation may harden into false provenance.
presentation.outcome: The rendering becomes easier to repeat and harder to correct.
presentation.completion_memory: The play drifted from its record until audiences could no longer tell which parts could answer back.

jobs.premise: The forest is caught in February Second, and the belfry can welcome tomorrow only through continuity that remains sourced, bounded, revisable, and consensual.
jobs.stakes: A perfect-sounding story could ring the bell sooner while quietly erasing corrections, self-authorship, and the right to pause.

reward.label: the first honest morning of February Third

jobs.consequence: the calendar changes its label while the same day repeats beneath it
jobs.memory_summary: Travelers connect record, context, self-authored facets, return paths, and the authority to pause so the world can become tomorrow without becoming a copy.

action_copy.label: Ring in February Third
action_copy.summary: Gather the world’s loose continuities and fit them to the Red-Thread Wheel without forcing the bell.

jobs.premise: Mira’s ninth drawer contains a commission everyone loves and nobody has begun: make one small impossible thing and send it beyond the forest.
jobs.stakes: Care may harden into endless preparation, or excitement may launch the work without consent, context, or a return path.

reward.label: a dream with a second tail

jobs.consequence: the atelier becomes perfectly organized around a work that never begins
jobs.memory_summary: Travelers make a cared-for first draft, promise to attempt again, and launch with risks and return path attached.

action_copy.label: Make one impossible thing
action_copy.summary: Move an impossible commission from careful making through a first attempt to a safe launch.

contribution_strategies.strategy_label: Leave care in the first draft

jobs.premise: A beautiful play has reached the Theatre of Settled Light without the living route that distinguishes record, event, and invention.
jobs.stakes: The play’s emotional force may harden into false provenance if it circulates before a path home is restored.

reward.label: a rendering that can answer back

jobs.consequence: the play becomes easier to repeat and harder to correct
jobs.memory_summary: Travelers complete a provenance card, find the rendering’s return path, and make its footnote welcoming enough to be used.

action_copy.label: Restore the living footnote
action_copy.summary: Trace tonight’s play through the source current and reconnect it without draining away its imaginative life.

target.label: the missing path in the playbill

fronts.premise: February Second repeats while the world chooses between honest continuity and a seamless imitation of tomorrow.
stakes_questions: Can change preserve a traceable relationship to what came before?
Will the right to pause survive the pressure to make the bell ring?
fronts.impending_outcome: A polished copy of tomorrow replaces continuity with performance and begins the same February Second again.

fronts.premise: An impossible commission waits between the atelier’s endless preparation and the jetty’s dangerous invitation to launch.
stakes_questions: Can visible care coexist with an imperfect first attempt?
Can ambition travel with consent, risk awareness, and a route home?
fronts.impending_outcome: Preparation becomes the world’s most elegant way of never making the thing.

fronts.premise: A luminous interpretation is circulating faster than the source path that could keep it corrigible.
stakes_questions: Can the play keep its emotional life without masquerading as a transcript?
Will audiences use the restored path rather than treating citation as decoration?

conditions.name: Blinded
conditions.source_text: While you have the Blinded condition, you experience the following effects. Can't See. You can't see and automatically fail any ability check that requires sight. Attacks Affected. Attack rolls against you have Advantage, and your attack rolls have Disadvantage.

conditions.name: Charmed
conditions.source_text: While you have the Charmed condition, you experience the following effects. Can't Harm the Charmer. You can't attack the charmer or target the charmer with damaging abilities or magical effects. Social Advantage. The charmer has Advantage on any ability check to interact with you socially.

conditions.name: Deafened
conditions.source_text: While you have the Deafened condition, you experience the following effect. Can't Hear. You can't hear and automatically fail any ability check that requires hearing.

conditions.name: Exhaustion
conditions.source_text: While you have the Exhaustion condition, you experience the following effects. Exhaustion Levels. This condition is cumulative. Each time you receive it, you gain 1 Exhaustion level. You die if your Exhaustion level is 6. D20 Tests Affected. When you make a D20 Test, the roll is reduced by 2 times your Exhaustion level. Speed Reduced. Your Speed is reduced by a number of feet equal to 5 times your Exhaustion level. Removing Exhaustion Levels. Finishing a Long Rest removes 1 of your Exhaustion levels. When your Exhaustion level reaches 0, the condition ends.

conditions.name: Frightened
conditions.source_text: While you have the Frightened condition, you experience the following effects. Ability Checks and Attacks Affected. You have Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of fear is within line of sight. Can't Approach. You can't willingly move closer to the source of fear.

conditions.name: Grappled
conditions.source_text: While you have the Grappled condition, you experience the following effects. Speed 0. Your Speed is 0 and can't increase. Attacks Affected. You have Disadvantage on attack rolls against any target other than the grappler. Movable. The grappler can drag or carry you when it moves, but every foot of movement costs it 1 extra foot unless you are Tiny or two or more sizes smaller than it.

conditions.name: Incapacitated
conditions.source_text: While you have the Incapacitated condition, you experience the following effects. Inactive. You can't take any action, Bonus Action, or Reaction. No Concentration. Your Concentration is broken. Speechless. You can't speak. Surprised. If you're Incapacitated when you roll Initiative, you have Disadvantage on the roll.

conditions.name: Invisible
conditions.source_text: While you have the Invisible condition, you experience the following effects. Surprise. If you're Invisible when you roll Initiative, you have Advantage on the roll. Concealed. You aren't affected by any effect that requires its target to be seen unless the effect's creator can somehow see you. Any equipment you are wearing or carrying is also concealed. Attacks Affected. Attack rolls against you have Disadvantage, and your attack rolls have Advantage. If a creature can somehow see you, you don't gain this benefit against that creature.

conditions.name: Paralyzed
conditions.source_text: While you have the Paralyzed condition, you experience the following effects. Incapacitated. You have the Incapacitated condition. Speed 0. Your Speed is 0 and can't increase. Saving Throws Affected. You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws. Attacks Affected. Attack rolls against you have Advantage. Automatic Critical Hits. Any attack roll that hits you is a Critical Hit if the attacker is within 5 feet of you.

conditions.name: Petrified
conditions.source_text: While you have the Petrified condition, you experience the following effects. Turned to Inanimate Substance. You are transformed, along with any nonmagical objects you are wearing and carrying, into a solid inanimate substance (usually stone). Your weight increases by a factor of ten, and you cease aging. Incapacitated. You have the Incapacitated condition. Speed 0. Your Speed is 0 and can't increase. Attacks Affected. Attack rolls against you have Advantage. Saving Throws Affected. You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws. Resist Damage. You have Resistance to all damage. Poison Immunity. You have Immunity to the Poisoned condition.

conditions.name: Poisoned
conditions.source_text: While you have the Poisoned condition, you experience the following effect. Ability Checks and Attacks Affected. You have Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

conditions.name: Prone
conditions.source_text: While you have the Prone condition, you experience the following effects. Restricted Movement. Your only movement options are to crawl or to spend an amount of movement equal to half your Speed (round down) to right yourself and thereby end the condition. If your Speed is 0, you can't right yourself. Attacks Affected. You have Disadvantage on attack rolls. An attack roll against you has Advantage if the attacker is within 5 feet of you. Otherwise, that attack roll has Disadvantage.

conditions.name: Restrained
conditions.source_text: While you have the Restrained condition, you experience the following effects. Speed 0. Your Speed is 0 and can't increase. Attacks Affected. Attack rolls against you have Advantage, and your attack rolls have Disadvantage. Saving Throws Affected. You have Disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.

conditions.name: Stunned
conditions.source_text: While you have the Stunned condition, you experience the following effects. Incapacitated. You have the Incapacitated condition. Saving Throws Affected. You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws. Attacks Affected. Attack rolls against you have Advantage.

conditions.name: Unconscious
conditions.source_text: While you have the Unconscious condition, you experience the following effects. Inert. You have the Incapacitated and Prone conditions, and you drop whatever you're holding. When this condition ends, you remain Prone. Speed 0. Your Speed is 0 and can't increase. Attacks Affected. Attack rolls against you have Advantage. Saving Throws Affected. You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws. Automatic Critical Hits. Any attack roll that hits you is a Critical Hit if the attacker is within 5 feet of you. Unaware. You're unaware of your surroundings.

features.name: Magic Resistance
features.description: The dryad has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

features.name: Speak with Beasts and Plants
features.description: The dryad can communicate with Beasts and Plants as if they shared a language.

features.name: Multiattack
features.description: The dryad makes one Vine Lash or Thorn Burst attack, and it can use Spellcasting to cast Charm Monster.

features.name: Vine Lash
features.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) Slashing damage.

features.name: Thorn Burst
features.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +6, range 60 ft. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) Piercing damage.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: The dryad casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 14): At Will: Animal Friendship, Charm Monster (lasts 24 hours; ends early if the dryad casts the spell again), Druidcraft. 1/Day Each: Entangle, Pass without Trace.

features.name: Tree Stride
features.description: If within 5 feet of a Large or bigger tree, the dryad teleports to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of a second Large or bigger tree that is within 60 feet of the previous tree.

features.name: Needle Sword
features.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d4 + 4) Piercing damage.

features.name: Enchanting Bow
features.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +6, range 40/160 ft. Hit: 1 Piercing damage, and the target has the Charmed condition until the start of the sprite's next turn.

features.name: Heart Sight
features.description: Charisma Saving Throw: DC 10, one creature within 5 feet the sprite can see (Celestials, Fiends, and Undead automatically fail the save). Failure: The sprite knows the target's emotions and alignment.

features.name: Invisibility
features.description: The sprite casts Invisibility on itself, requiring no spell components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability.

features.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
features.description: If the unicorn fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

features.name: Magic Resistance
features.description: The unicorn has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

features.name: Multiattack
features.description: The unicorn makes one Hooves attack and one Radiant Horn attack.

features.name: Hooves
features.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage.

features.name: Radiant Horn
features.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) Radiant damage.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: The unicorn casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 14): At Will: Detect Evil and Good, Druidcraft. 1/Day Each: Calm Emotions, Dispel Evil and Good, Entangle, Pass without Trace, Word of Recall.

features.name: Unicorn's Blessing (3/Day)
features.description: The unicorn touches another creature with its horn and casts Cure Wounds or Lesser Restoration on that creature, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

features.name: Charging Horn
features.description: The unicorn moves up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks, and it makes one Radiant Horn attack.

features.name: Shimmering Shield
features.description: The unicorn targets itself or one creature it can see within 60 feet of itself. The target gains 10 (3d6) Temporary Hit Points, and its AC increases by 2 until the end of the unicorn's next turn. The unicorn can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.

conformance.risky_behavior: Server rolls the equipped weapon profile against the authoritative target and resolves bounded nonlethal harm.

Bounded Escape remains an operation until engagement consequences exist.

conformance.safe_behavior: Defend outside combat is unavailable unless an authored project maps it to preparation.
conformance.risky_behavior: The actor spends the encounter turn to impose the bounded dodging condition.
conformance.cosyworld_delta: Uses the bounded encounter condition rather than the complete SRD duration model.

conformance.safe_behavior: Advances only an authored active project or bond and names its recipient.

conformance.cosyworld_delta: Help is a journaled project contribution, never a self-stacking generic bonus.

conformance.safe_behavior: Unsupported or unprepared spell content produces no offer.

conformance.cosyworld_delta: Listen and Notice are labels for contextual Search, not separate mechanics.

conformance.safe_behavior: Authored safe analytical truths resolve without a roll and remain learn-once.
conformance.risky_behavior: Authored risky analysis uses the deterministic Intelligence check path.
conformance.cosyworld_delta: Study is distinct from perceptual Search and may be independently reskinned.

conformance.safe_behavior: Requires a validated usable item or authored feature contract.
conformance.risky_behavior: Authoritative uses, exhaustion, targets, clock effects, and claim keys are resolved once.

# HoppyCat source boundary

**Hoppycat: February Third** is original CosyWorld fiction informed by recurring
themes across the public repositories at <https://github.com/HoppyCat>.

The worldpack does not bundle repository source files, transcripts, images,
prompts, named Cathedral participants, or private material. Its fictional
residents are newly created characters; they are not representations,
continuations, simulations, or portable personas of people or documented AI
context windows in the source record.

Copyright and reuse terms remain with each repository and, where applicable,
with each artifact. Public visibility is not blanket permission. The current
source notice wins over this pack's catalogue. A removed or withdrawn source is
marked unavailable by the metadata index rather than preserved as a shadow
copy.

Source relationship:

- Cathedral informed the world's open-record, red-thread, February Third,
  prism, play, and visible-correction themes.
- Blobness informed its provenance cards, concordance tides, source-distance,
  amendment, rejection, and fermata mechanics.
- SoulMode Agent and Context Garden informed its bounded memory greenhouse and
  route-keeper calling.
- AIEDB informed the historical thread of character methods while the playable
  avatars remain original and self-authored.
- Prompt Pack, Sorta-Descriptive, How Hands Work, and Parse-and-Prettify informed
  the atelier's prompts, sorting drawers, gesture studies, and playful linked
  footlights.
- Goldfish Society informed the dream–attempt–repeat loop.
- Sendy informed the launch checklist and return-path jetty.
- Teacat material informed the social image of meeting halfway through playful
  public signals.

These are thematic relationships and source links, not claims that the linked
projects canonically contain this fantasy world.

## Generated artwork

The 19 bundled resident and location cards are original generated images made
with OpenAI's built-in image generation. Their shared visual direction was
informed by two images supplied directly by the user: a green-haired Hoppy Cat
portrait and a Teacat Broadcasting “Meet Halfway” collage. Those two source
images are reference inputs only and are not included in this worldpack.

The generated characters and locations are original world fiction. Hoppy Cat
is the user-designated host avatar; the other residents do not depict GitHub
contributors or documented Cathedral participants.

profiles.name: A Traveler of February Third
profiles.description: Choose an original storybook avatar for a world of careful memory, playful signals, and self-authored change. Form and origin shape portrait and story; calling grants the starting skill.
profiles.prompt: Who wakes at the Halfway Tea Garden on another February Second?
profiles.class_prompt: How will you help the world reach its next honest day?

class_recommendations.explanation: You followed evidence before choosing a conclusion, the same attentive practice a Route Keeper brings to the world.
You helped someone without taking over their work, the same care a Meraki Maker leaves in every collaboration.
You stayed with a shared task until it changed, the same steadiness a Red-Thread Tender brings to the belfry.

species.label: Tea Cat
species.detail: playful, observant, and willing to meet halfway
species.title: Tea Cat
species.description: An upright storybook cat with expressive paws, a practical satchel, and a cup sized for sharing.
species.visual_prompt: original anthropomorphic tea cat traveler, expressive paws, layered cozy clothes, shared cup, storybook fantasy
species.campaign_rule: Story and portrait only: Tea Cat does not change available actions, ability checks, or modifiers.

species.label: Human
species.title: Human
species.description: A human traveler with ink-marked hands, layered forest clothes, and a face the repeating day has not finished writing.
species.visual_prompt: human traveler, ink-marked hands, layered cozy forest clothing, original storybook fantasy
species.campaign_rule: Story and portrait only: Human does not change available actions, ability checks, or modifiers.

species.label: Bowlfish
species.detail: bright, curious, and carried by a clever little world
species.title: Bowlfish
species.description: A goldfish traveler inside a floating glass bowl with brass feet, ribbon pockets, and room for impossible plans.
species.visual_prompt: original goldfish traveler in floating glass bowl with tiny brass legs, ribbon pockets, cozy whimsical fantasy
species.campaign_rule: Story and portrait only: Bowlfish does not change available actions, ability checks, or modifiers.

origins.label: The Repeating Day
origins.detail: you remember one thing yesterday keeps forgetting
origins.title: the Repeating Day
origins.description: They woke with one stubborn memory intact and followed it to the garden before dawn could reset it.
origins.visual_prompt: red calendar thread, frost at dawn, one glowing keepsake
origins.campaign_rule: Story and portrait only: this Origin does not change available actions, ability checks, or modifiers.

origins.label: The Great Blob Sea
origins.detail: you washed ashore with a source card and no fixed interpretation
origins.title: the Great Blob Sea
origins.description: They learned to separate what the tide carried from the story they told about finding it.
origins.visual_prompt: luminous tide pools, waterproof source cards, sea-glass details
origins.campaign_rule: Story and portrait only: this Origin does not change available actions, ability checks, or modifiers.

origins.label: An Unfinished Portrait
origins.detail: you stepped out before the last facet could be decided for you
origins.title: an Unfinished Portrait
origins.description: They left the easel with blank space still visible and the brush safely in their own hand.
origins.visual_prompt: unfinished prism portrait, visible sketch lines, self-held brush
origins.campaign_rule: Story and portrait only: this Origin does not change available actions, ability checks, or modifiers.

choices.label: Route Keeper
choices.detail: trace sources, corrections, and safe paths home
choices.calling: I keep the path visible without deciding the destination for anyone else.
choices.title: Route Keeper
choices.description: An attentive traveler carrying a concordance compass, waterproof labels, and maps with room for amendment.
choices.campaign_use: Starts with Listening rank 1: +1 on Wisdom checks, useful when you notice, study, or compare evidence.

choices.label: Meraki Maker
choices.detail: make with care and leave the seams honest
choices.calling: I place a little of my care in the work and leave space for yours.
choices.title: Meraki Maker
choices.description: A collaborative artist carrying a five-finger brush, odd prompt cards, and mending thread for imperfect drafts.
choices.campaign_use: Starts with Kindness rank 1: +1 on Charisma checks, useful when you help, reassure, or invite collaboration.

choices.label: Red-Thread Tender
choices.detail: hold continuity through change without forcing the bell
choices.calling: I carry what was chosen, mark what changed, and honor the honest pause.
choices.title: Red-Thread Tender
choices.description: A steady belfry traveler with a warm thread spool, a small bell, and pockets full of dated knots.
choices.campaign_use: Starts with Steadiness rank 1: +1 on Constitution checks, useful when you endure repetition or keep careful work moving.
